**Strategy:** Broad-to-narrow. Start with name + place + date range. If a batch number surfaces, I'll re-search within the batch to enumerate all Richardson baptisms in the window and look for family patterning (same parents recurring across siblings). I'll pass `subjectId: "I1"` throughout — the tree person is sparse, but ranking will still help sort candidates.

13,069 total matches — exactly what the plan warned about. The top two results are both from Ashton-under-Lyne on 25 Sep 1832, from different batch numbers (I03213-6 and C00558-7). Let me read both immediately to check for parent names, and also look at the batch numbers — that's the key to enumerating the whole Ashton register.

Important findings from the two reads:
- **NFCY-7VM** (batch I03213-6): Christening 25 Sep 1832 — only shows a parent named "Mary" (indexed Male — likely an indexing error on sex)
- **JMF4-CL9** (batch C00558-7): Christening 25 Sep 1832, St. Michael and All Angels — **Father: Thomas Richardson, Mother: Mary** — much richer data

These appear to be the same entry indexed twice. Both are 25 Sep **1832**, not 1833 — a notable date discrepancy against the objective. Before adopting this family, I need to work the batch for St. Michael's to see whether another John Richardson appears closer to 1833, and to look for siblings confirming which Thomas+Mary family is the right one. Searching batch C00558-7 for all Richardsons now:

This batch search is gold. It returned all **30** Richardson records in the St. Michael and All Angels batch — a complete enumeration of one Ashton church's register. Let me quickly map the families before logging, so I know what to cross-check.

**Family patterns in batch C00558-7:**

| Child | Baptism date | Father (co-person) | Notes |

Critical observation: The **only John Richardson baptism** in this entire St. Michael's batch is 25 Sep **1832** — son of **Thomas Richardson + Mary**. The November 1834 cluster is a mass adult baptism of an unrelated "John Richardson Sr." family (children born 1807–1827). 

The 1832 date vs the objective's "1833" is a real discrepancy but consistent with census rounding (a child baptised Sep 1832 could appear as "born 1833" in a census taken in 1841/1851 if he gave age to the nearest year). This needs checking — but first I need to verify whether batch I03213-6 is a different Ashton church or a duplicate index of St. Michael's. Logging both searches now, then checking I03213-6.

Good — log_001 and log_002 written. Now update pli_001 status and check batch I03213-6:

Batch I03213-6 is a smaller extract — only 5 records, covering a different (or overlapping) Ashton source. Crucially:

- New data: Anne Richardson (1 Apr 1832) and Helen Richardson (4 Nov 1832) — both with father **James Richardson**, a different family — no John Richardson candidate here

I now have a complete picture. Let me log this third search, then present the full findings.

All three searches logged (log_001 through log_003). Here is the complete picture.

## Search results — pli_001: John Richardson baptism, Ashton-under-Lyne 1830–1836

### What was searched
Three progressive searches, each with its own log entry:

| Log | Search | Results |
|---|---|---|
| log_001 | Name search: John Richardson, baptism, Ashton-under-Lyne, 1830–1836 | 13,069 total; top 2 hits from Ashton, rest from elsewhere in Lancashire |
| log_002 | Batch C00558-7 (St Michael and All Angels): all Richardsons | 30 records — complete batch enumeration |
| log_003 | Batch I03213-6 (second Ashton index): all Richardsons | 5 records — complete batch enumeration |

### One candidate, and only one

Across both indexed Ashton-under-Lyne batches, there is exactly **one John Richardson baptism** in the FamilySearch index:

> **John Richardson**, christened **25 Sep 1832**, Church of St Michael and All Angels, Ashton-under-Lyne, Lancashire
> **Father:** Thomas Richardson | **Mother:** Mary (maiden name not indexed)
> Collection 1473014 — *England, Births and Christenings, 1538-1975*
> ARK: `ark:/61903/1:1:JMF4-CL9` (matchScore 0.68 against I1)

The same entry appears in batch I03213-6 (NFCY-7VM) — a second, less-complete indexing of the same register entry that captured only the mother's name and missed the father. These are the same record, not two different Johns.

### The date discrepancy — noting it, not dismissing it

The objective records "bapt. 1833"; the register entry is **25 Sep 1832**. That is a ~15-month gap from the objective's nominal year, but the discrepancy almost certainly flows from the *source* of "1833" — most likely a census return where John stated an age that implied birth ~1833, or a rough approximation. The baptism register is the original source; its date takes precedence. A child baptised September 1832 could plausibly appear as "age 8" in the June 1841 census (which would imply birth ~1833), or "age 18" in the March 1851 census (likewise). The discrepancy is within ordinary census-rounding range, and this is the only candidate in the entire indexed register.

### The November 1834 mass baptism group — ruled out, correctly

The other large cluster in St Michael's batch — multiple children (Dorcas, James, Anne, Peter, Joseph, William, Henry, Phoebe) all bearing "John Richardson" as father and all baptised on a single day in November 1834 — is a mass adult baptism: the birth dates on those entries span 1807–1827. That is a different, unrelated family being brought into the church of record simultaneously. No child named John Richardson appears in that group.

| Date plausible | ✓ 25 Sep 1832 — consistent with census-derived "~1833" |

| Both parents named | ✓ Father Thomas Richardson, Mother Mary |
| Attached to subject | Not yet — new evidence |
| Logical role check | ✓ Principal; no role conflict |

Any household structure will be inferred from surname, age, and listing order. Patrick is person `I1`, born ~1845 in Ireland. Executing the search now against collection 1438024.

A collection mismatch has come back — the single result is from the **1850 census** (collection 1401638), not 1870. This is the Patrick Flynn / Thomas Flynn household already known to this project. The 1870 collection (1438024) returned nothing matching. Let me log that finding.

Logged as **log_006**. Here's the full picture:

---

## 1870 Census Search — Patrick Flynn, Schuylkill County, PA

**Search executed:** United States Census, 1870 (collection 1438024) · surname Flynn · given name Patrick · Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania · residence year 1870 · birth year 1840–1850

**Result: Collection mismatch**

The one record FamilySearch returned is from the **1850 census** (collection 1401638) — the already-documented Patrick Flynn listed in a dwelling with Thomas Flynn and others (family structure inferred from surname, age, and listing order, not stated by the 1850 schedule). No 1870 census entry for Patrick Flynn in Schuylkill County was surfaced by FamilySearch's indexed search against collection 1438024.

This mismatch pattern — the engine surfacing a 1850 record when explicitly targeted at 1870 — is a FamilySearch indexing/routing quirk, not a spelling problem. **Name variants will not fix it.**

---

### What this means
The FamilySearch-indexed 1870 census for Schuylkill County did not return a matching Patrick Flynn. Two interpretations are possible:
1. **He was there but is not findable via FamilySearch's 1870 index** — a transcription error in the index (e.g., name garbled), or the household head's name was enumerated and indexed rather than Patrick's.
2. **He was not in Schuylkill County in 1870** — he may have been working in a neighboring county's mines, or had already started an independent household elsewhere.

### Suggested next steps
- **Ancestry's 1870 census** — independently indexed and supports partial/phonetic matching, which can surface records FamilySearch's exact index misses. The `search-external-sites` skill can generate the URL.
- **Broaden to Pennsylvania state level** — drop the county filter and search all of Pennsylvania, in case Patrick had moved to an adjacent coal county (Carbon, Columbia, Northumberland).

## 1860 Census — George Ackerman, Pennsylvania: What the Record Shows About the Marriage

### The search
I ran a new ad-hoc search against the 1860 US Federal Census (FamilySearch collection 1473181) for **George Ackerman** in Pennsylvania, anchored on wife **Catherine**. One result returned — George Ackerman in **Bucks County** (ARK `M7QZ-8KD`). A prior search (log_001) had already found a second George Ackerman household in **Berks County** (ARK `M4QZ-7YT`). Both are in the same 1860 census collection.

---

### What the record shows

| Person | Age | Birth Year (est.) | Birthplace |
|---|---|---|---|
| George Ackerman (head) | 42 | ~1818 | Pennsylvania |
| Henry Ackerman | 9 | ~1851 | Pennsylvania |
| Margaret Ackerman | 6 | ~1854 | Pennsylvania |

**Catherine is not in the household.** The spouse field was searched explicitly — `relativeTerms.spouse: absent` confirms she is not named anywhere on the record. No wife appears.

---

### What the 1860 schedule recorded (and what it did not)

The 1860 federal population schedule collected **name, age, sex, occupation, real- and personal-estate value, birthplace, and a "married within the year" checkbox**. It did **not** collect:
- Relationship to head (that column debuted in **1880**)
- Marriage date or marriage place
- Parents' birthplaces

So the census cannot directly answer when or where George and Catherine married. The "married within the year" checkbox was **not triggered** for this household.

---

### What the record tells us about the marriage — and what is inferred

| Finding | Basis | Status |
|---|---|---|
| George and Catherine were married **before ~1851** | If Henry (age 9 in 1860) is their child, they were married by ~1850–51 at the latest | **Inferred** from household position and shared surname — no relationship column in 1860 |
| Catherine likely **predeceased** the 1860 census | No wife is present; George is apparently a widower | **Inferred** from absence; confirmed by no other household adult female listed |
| Catherine was alive and bore Margaret **ca. 1854** | Margaret (age 6) would have been born ~1854, still within the marriage | **Inferred** — same caveats on parentage |
| Marriage date, place, and Catherine's maiden name | Not collected by the 1860 schedule | **Cannot be determined** from this record |

> ⚠️ **Critical caveat — pre-1880 census, no relationship column.** Henry and Margaret's status as George's children is an *inference* from their shared surname and listing position in the household. The enumerator stated no relationships. This inference is reasonable but not stated by the record.

---

### Bottom line

The 1860 census is **silent on the marriage itself** — it records no date, place, or spouse name. Catherine's most significant appearance is her *absence*: she is not in the household, which is consistent with her having died sometime between Margaret's birth (~1854) and the census date (June 1860). To document the marriage directly, you would need a marriage record, church register, or a census year when both George and Catherine were enumerated together (the 1850 census would be the natural next step).
